model.architecture: Fully-hybrid Falcon-H1 (every layer runs a grouped-query attention branch and a Mamba2 selective-scan branch in parallel); the Deep variant trades width for depth — 66 layers at hidden size 1280 — so the bundle carries 264 state buffers (132 conv/SSM + 132 KV).

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic on linears + embedding (convs and the scan stay float); fp32 activations declared for GPU

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 7.71 tok/s decode / 138.4 prefill, peak 3745 MB, init 89.0 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-24, 1 run) against CPU 11.27-11.97 decode / 87.6-103.1 prefill, peak 3630 MB, init 6.0 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: the CPU decodes 1.5x faster than the GPU on this handset, so the earlier GPU choice is reversed; gpu keeps the prefill advantage for prompt-heavy, short-output work

platform_notes: GPU runs with fp32 activations (declared in the bundle) — expect a corresponding memory multiple over CPU.
Depth costs decode: 66 sequential attention+scan blocks per token; decode lands below the shallower 3B sibling while prefill comes out ahead.

The full prefill ladder loads on a 12 GB phone with all 264 state buffers: GPU peak 4.89 GB (2.8× the file); load takes about a minute on GPU (8 s on CPU) because Metal kernels for every signature are built at engine creation.
Multi-length prefill signatures (1–1024) are exported so the runtime picks tight chunks; the bundle carries the tokenizer and the stock ChatML-style Falcon-H1 chat template.
Usage example runs the GPU backend with `--backend gpu --cache no`.

Not a measured row: card reports iPhone 17 Pro gpu prefill_tps 140.3, decode_tps 16.5, ttft_s 1.19 (Performance — On device table (iPhone 17 Pro, cold start, single runs); runtime/run count not stated)

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (115393 ops across 12 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: On GPU the runtime logs `TopK requires src tensor C dimension to be divisible by 4` (vocab 65537) — a fallback path, not a failure; generation and quality gates unaffected.
iPhone 17 Pro: GPU and CPU answers differ by one function word ("8 times 7 equals 56" on GPU, "is 56" on CPU).
